transcript:
Header: Tue Dec 02 2025 | Start 14:30 PST | Duration ~54m
Attendees: Lena Morales (Redwood AE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Iris Cole (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Borealis Platform), Diego Alvarez (Borealis ML), Priya Singh (Borealis PM), Arun Patel (Borealis Security)

00:00 Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we left a little buffer so we can run through the safety window and the slos, quick check - any new blockers?
00:07 Maya: no blockers, just wanted to confirm staging's traffic mirror is set up, we saw a few dropped requests yesterday on the mirror but not on prod mimic, so we want to be careful with the canary traffic size.
00:15 Samir: yeah I saw that too - probably a mirror mesh issue, not Redwood, but still we should plan smaller initial ramp.
00:22 Priya: smaller initial ramp sounds good — what are you suggesting numerically?
00:26 Samir: propose 1% baseline for first 30 minutes, then 5% for next hour if p95 latency under 700ms and error-rate <0.5%. then jump to 20% for two hours if stable. It's conservative but buys safety.
00:40 Diego: are those thresholds token-cost aware? our cost buckets spike when sequence length goes up.
00:47 Samir: good point — we can gate on both latency and token-per-request moving average. maybe p95 <700ms and token avg delta <15% vs control.
00:56 Arun: from security side, we need to lock down the KMS rotation window; we can't have key rotations during canary. also audit logs must be available in near-real-time, like within 15 mins.
01:05 Lena: noted. Iris, can you remind the audit log doc link we shared?
01:08 Iris: sure, I posted the security pack in the shared notes - "redwood-security-audit-v2.pdf". will put a direct link after the call.
01:15 Priya: on rollback policies - if model regresses on quality metrics we want automatic fallback to the previous stable model for at least 10 minutes while we triage. is that supported?
01:23 Samir: yes, automated fallback is supported. we can configure an A/B style gate or a hard rollback. for your flow i recommend A/B gate where 100% of failing requests route to the stable model and we pause ramp. but we can do immediate hard rollback if you prefer.
01:36 Diego: what's the difference in state for KV cache and sessions when we fallback? do we lose context?
01:41 Samir: good question - if you fall back to the older model variant the KV cache keys are compatible across minor versions but not across major architecture changes. i'll annotate that in the playbook.
01:52 Maya: that's important — we have long-prompt sessions in telehealth transcripts so we need cache persistency obviously.
01:57 Lena: also, monitoring — what dashboards do you want? latency, error rate, token cost, quality (BLEU-ish or semantic similarity), and business metrics right?
02:06 Priya: yes, business metrics: conversion on patient follow-ups, completion rate. but initial gating should be purely infra + quality.
02:13 Samir: I will share a compact dashboard template: p50/p95 latency, errors per minute, token throughput, average tokens per request, top-5 degraded prompts by similarity delta.
02:25 Diego: can you include example tracing spans? our SREs want to correlate request-level traces with model inference spans.
02:29 Samir: yes, example spans and a suggested sampling rate. we'll include a note on OTLP vs our native collector — there was some mis-compat there earlier, the trunk collector string was wrong in staging and caused missed spans.
02:42 Priya: what's the planned dry-run date for the rollback and cutover?
02:46 Lena: we suggested a dry-run 2025-12-10, 14:00 PST. Sound ok?
02:51 Maya: works for us, i'll book it.
02:54 Arun: on compliance, do you keep a tamper-evident audit trail for admin actions? we need chain-of-custody for access to keys and model promotions.
03:02 Samir: we keep audit logs for admin actions and model promotions; they are signed and retained per your policy. we'll add an appendix showing the retention and tamper controls.
03:12 Priya: timeline wise, if dry-run goes well we aim cutover 2025-12-15 in the maintenance window. We need the final runbook at least 48 hours prior.
03:21 Lena: ok we will target runbook delivery by 2025-12-13. Samir will own the canary playbook doc.
03:26 Samir: i'll include traffic percentages, SLO gates, observable queries, rollback scripts, and a checklist for the SRE on-call.
03:36 Maya: regarding observability alerts, we want a pre-alert at 60% of threshold and an urgent page at 100% - can we map those?
03:42 Samir: yes, we'll provide Prometheus alert rules and example PagerDuty routing keys (we won't store keys in the doc).
03:48 Diego: one more question — function/tool calling or structured outputs, do we need to do anything special for A/B? like different response shapes?
03:55 Samir: you can run A/B with a simple adapter that normalizes outputs. if shape differs we'll transform to the canonical shape before passing to downstream. i'll add a snippet.
04:03 Priya: Are there any known gotchas for private VPC deployments — egress/ingress ports, or HSM network considerations?
04:09 Samir: yes, HSM traffic often needs dedicated routes and specific MTU configs; we had one customer with intermittent hangs due to MTU mismatch. we will list required ports and MTU recommendations in the ops appendix.
04:18 Arun: make sure the HSM vendor contact is on the runbook — if we need to coordinate key escrow there's a process.
04:24 Iris: i'll put the vendor contact and a high-level contact matrix in the runbook template.
04:30 Lena: quick check on metrics for quality regressions — what threshold do we use? Diego?
04:34 Diego: for semantic similarity i propose a 0.08 drop on average similarity vs baseline over a 15-minute window as a trigger. it's tight but for patient safety we need to be conservative.
04:44 Priya: okay that seems reasonable, let's codify it.
04:47 Lena: recap: Samir to draft canary playbook and dashboards by 12-05; Lena will share runbook skeleton and security appendix by 12-04; Maya to run staging smoke test 12-08 and confirm mirror stability; dry-run 12-10 at 14:00 PST; cutover tentatively 12-15.
05:03 Priya: sounds good, thanks everyone.
05:06 Lena: thanks all, we'll follow up in the notes with links. bye.

Auto-generated notes: Links mentioned: redwood-security-audit-v2.pdf (to be attached), compact-canary-playbook-draft.md (to be shared by Samir), grafana-dashboard-examples.json (to be shared by Lena).

Action items (recap): Samir - canary playbook by 2025-12-05; Lena - runbook skeleton + security appendix by 2025-12-04; Maya - staging smoke test results by 2025-12-08; Arun - confirm KMS/rotation window by 2025-12-09.
